site_changes.title: Represent the named people without losing existing profiles
site_changes.decision: Retained all 34 previously audited profiles. Added Danny Deep, Tommy Fisher, Robert Mauch, Steven Collis, Craig Abod, Stephen Budorick, Darrell Crate and Pat Gelsinger from the new people and company ledgers. Retained Shyam Sankar and the correct John Heller/Amentum identity. The result is 42 profiles and 39 indexed companies, not the package’s 39 people.
site_changes.remaining: This is a selected research cohort, not a census of government beneficiaries.

site_changes.title: Corporate parent totals and the McKesson discrepancy
site_changes.decision: Retained the exact transaction-based USAspending snapshot. McKesson UEI S1RUKWWRYFL6 has $9,529,383,500.37 FY2023 net obligations. That record does not identify the source of the old negative $507.3M figure. The package provides no reproducible parent-membership bridge for the $64.726B Lockheed Martin or $25.405B UnitedHealth claims, so those consolidated totals remain withheld.
site_changes.remaining: Exact API requests/responses, dated subsidiary membership, transaction IDs and provenance of the negative McKesson rollup.

site_changes.title: Pfizer, PIP and malformed source rows
site_changes.decision: The site already distinguishes ENT_PIP (PIP Manufacturing) and ENT_PFE (Pfizer). The new ledger does not establish the claimed $8.431B reallocation with a verified UEI/award bridge. Original malformed workbooks remain intact for provenance; their repair is not treated as proof that their financial values are correct.
site_changes.remaining: Primary identifiers and award-level evidence for PIP and Pfizer; a machine-readable source-row repair map.

site_changes.title: Separate ownership, funds and personal proceeds
site_changes.decision: Unknown private compensation, distributions, stakes and carried interest remain null. Company obligations and managed client assets are not personal income. The 2021 Perspecta proxy supports historical Veritas Funds V/VII links, not a verified current Fund VIII allocation or Musallam’s personal carry.
site_changes.remaining: Dated fund-to-company ownership, economic allocations, distributions and private cap tables.

site_changes.title: Bechtel National’s Hanford earned fee
site_changes.decision: Published the $14,208,000 CY2024 earned award fee for the Hanford WTP High-Level Waste Facility portion, against a $15M available pool. Rejected the derived 0.34% “net margin”: the supplied obligation denominator is not reconciled to the same contract portion, period or accounting basis. An earned fee does not establish company net profit or a personal distribution.
site_changes.remaining: Matched cost, obligation and payment records; any allocation to Bechtel owners.

site_changes.title: Longview’s dated portfolio transactions
site_changes.decision: Primary records place the transactions in 2026. The full exhibit spans September 1–October 1; only September’s 2,638,137 shares, about $930.69M at reported prices, fall inside the window. October 1’s 69,734 shares are excluded. The 2,546,119-share snapshot decline is a different calculation. No personal Crown-family proceeds are assigned.
site_changes.remaining: Client-level economic interests and actual distributions; net proceeds after expenses and taxes.

site_changes.title: Palantir voting and Thiel’s March sale
site_changes.decision: Retained joint Class F voting-control treatment. Added approximately $289.71M gross sale value from 2M shares sold March 2, 2026 by STS Holdings II LLC, whose sole beneficial owner is Thiel. It is a sale-value measure, separate from compensation, capital gain and net personal cash.
site_changes.remaining: Cost basis, taxes, fees, distributions and the rest of the four-year sale history.

site_changes.title: Executive pay and Beck’s sale records
site_changes.decision: Retained verified SCT totals instead of replacing them with the new ledger’s rounded or incorrect values. Beck’s March code-S tax-cover sale is about $1.31M. Equatorial Trust’s July sales are about $286.41M; the filing does not allocate the whole trust amount to Beck personally. These are separate records, not a $287.72M personal-cash total.
site_changes.remaining: Complete sale history, trust economic allocation and reconciliation of the older $429.6M claim.

site_changes.title: Spice’s compensation and realized equity
site_changes.decision: Retained $455,090 FY2025 SCT compensation and $102,066,233 of option-exercise spread plus stock-vesting value. The latter does not prove shares were sold or cash received. Rejected the workbook’s label “Total Net Realized” and its claim that 99.6% of wealth came from stock appreciation.
site_changes.remaining: Original Form 4 rows reconciled by transaction type, date and amended filing; the $145.7M claim remains unresolved.

site_changes.title: Build a graph that matches the published directory
site_changes.decision: The supplied JSON has 14 edges and no nodes, despite the workbook’s 78-node completeness claim. The site now generates a complete node index from its 42 profiles and 39 company entries, with typed, sourced company-to-person relationships. These links describe research relationships; they do not imply personal receipt of company awards.
site_changes.remaining: Verified ownership layers, joint-venture economics and agency-to-award links beyond the selected cohort.

site_changes.title: State incentive totals
site_changes.decision: The new $366.2M sum reclassifies source fields as state grants and tax abatements without primary state records. Arithmetic alone cannot validate that reclassification or resolve the original $40.320B discrepancy. Neither total is published as verified public incentives.
site_changes.remaining: Program-by-program primary records, jurisdiction, funding type, period and additive reconciliation.

site_changes.title: Date the oversight findings accurately
site_changes.decision: Retained the already-audited GAO coverage dates and definitions. The package again describes SBIR percentages as commercialization or transition rates; this does not replace the site’s source-based reporting-coverage interpretation. OTA reporting gaps are not established theft or personal benefit.
site_changes.remaining: Updated official follow-up reports and consistent definitions for each reporting gap.

site_changes.title: Add omitted recipients and spending channels
site_changes.decision: Added six companies to the index and linked their named people. Highlighted Fisher and AmerisourceBergen’s exact single-UEI snapshot values. Added verified REIT compensation and Intel’s amended funding terms. Withheld unsubstantiated annual totals and UEIs for Carahsoft, COPT, Easterly and Intel. The proposed $27B discovery sum is not a supported additive total.
site_changes.remaining: Actual award/payment exports, GSA lease reconciliation, reseller pass-throughs and current recipient identifiers.

site_changes.title: Executive compensation cost allowability
site_changes.decision: A compensation cost limit does not trace the funding of an executive’s pay. SEC SCT values and allowable contract costs have different definitions. Subtracting an assumed cap from SCT cannot show that 95%+ of pay came from commercial activity; company profit can also arise from government contracts.
site_changes.remaining: Applicable contract terms, year-specific rules, exceptions and actual cost-allocation/reimbursement records.

additional_findings: The people ledger omits Shyam Sankar and misidentifies John Heller of Amentum as “Stephen Heller” at CACI. Those regressions were not imported.

Already-verified FY2025 SCT totals were preserved: Taiclet $23,453,308; Novakovic $25,924,082; Warden $25,357,443; Ortberg $23,581,389. The new ledger supplied different amounts without matching primary tables.
Danny Deep’s verified FY2025 SCT is $8,394,711, not $8.5M. His October 2026 CEO appointment is outside the spending window; the profile uses his in-window president/operating-executive role.
The memo’s $14.2B Hanford fee is a 1,000-fold unit error. The primary scorecard shows $14.208M for a defined facility portion.
Beck’s March filing uses transaction code S for sell-to-cover. Tax withholding purpose is preserved without relabeling the transaction as code F.
Beck’s 2025 vesting and 2026 trust sales are not added to form a personal-benefit total. Transaction events can relate to the same shares and different beneficial interests.
Intel’s $769M 2025 capital-incentive recognition is not its total CHIPS cash disbursement. The amended award and government share transaction require separate accounting.
The supplied negative-search log asserts searches but does not provide complete reproducible raw results. Its claims of exhaustive coverage, zero awards or active monitoring are not adopted.

The new company ledger contains unsupported round annual values and unverified identifiers. Only the precise existing USAspending snapshot observations and independently checked company disclosures are used.

channels.limits: $13,353,127,851.70 from the November 12 snapshot. FY2026 reporting remains incomplete. Rank is within that query, not a consolidated corporate-parent ranking.

channels.question: Which buildings, ownership entities and joint ventures receive federal rent—and what remains after property costs?
channels.limits: These are annual reported pay packages, including grant-date awards. No federal rental total or share of pay funded by federal tenants has been established here.

channels.measure: CY2024 earned award fee · HLW Facility portion
channels.finding: DOE awarded 94.7% of the $15M available fee pool for the specified portion of the project. A fee is closer to retained economics than a gross award, but it still is not personal income.
channels.question: What do matched cost and payment records show, and is any distribution to owners publicly documented?
channels.limits: This scorecard does not establish net profit, fee cash payment, a whole-contract margin, or Brendan Bechtel’s personal benefit. The report’s 0.34% margin was rejected.
